summary: Build the SOX Protocol conformance suite: declarative YAML fixtures covering all 12 fixture categories spanning the 16 v1 operations and 7 primitives, a Python harness (tools/conformance_runner.py) that runs each fixture against either the in-process Python reference impl (target=packages/python, stdio) or a remote HTTP target (target=http://host:port), and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs both targets on every PR. The runner consumes the http-transport's SSE stream at GET /v1/stream for live recv arrivals (matching the http-transport plan's wire_format choice). The harness has 100% unit-test coverage. Existing JSON scenarios under spec/conformance/scenarios/ are migrated to the new YAML category layout to avoid duplication.

schema.name: human-readable fixture name
schema.pending: optional bool; if true, runner skips in --strict mode (used for x-status: planned operations like channels_collect)
schema.setup: list of {operation, input} executed in order before the test sequence; responses ignored unless asserted via expected_setup_output
schema.agents: list of {id, credential} virtual agents the runner authenticates as; each step references which agent runs it
schema.sequence: ordered list of {as_agent, operation, input, expected_output (subset match with seq/message_id wildcards), expected_error (sox-error envelope match), wait_for_stream (optional SSE assertion: {channel, seq_at_least, timeout_s})}
schema.teardown: optional list of operations for cleanup

fixtures.purpose: Single-channel send by agent A; agent B subscribed receives via recv with seq=1.
recv with no pending messages returns empty list, non-blocking.
include_meta:false omits _meta block; include_meta:true includes trace_id.
subscribe pattern team/* receives team/eng but not ops/eng.
unsubscribe drops queued-but-unread messages for the removed pattern.
Multiple overlapping subscriptions deliver each message exactly once.
send with reply_to threads to parent message_id; recv with thread_depth surfaces parent context.
3-level deep thread; thread_depth=2 returns 2 ancestors.
group_create -> group_invite -> group_join transitions invitee from invited to active; group_list_members reflects membership.
send to a group channel fans out to all active members; non-members do not receive.
group_leave removes member; subsequent broadcasts do not deliver.
DM channel name is dm/<sorted-pair>; same channel regardless of which agent sent first.
Agent C subscribed to dm/* cannot read messages between A and B.
channels_ack is invoked as a tool; the ack does NOT appear in channel history on subsequent recv.
channels_ack with status=nack records NACK; pending-state reflects rejection; no body posted to channel.
Sender field in stored envelope is server-certified from auth credential, not from client-supplied body.
send with unrecognized credential returns sox-error; no message persisted.
First message in a fresh channel has seq=1; recv echoes it.
10 sends produce seq 1..10; recv returns them in seq order; second channel's seq sequence is independent.
channels_heartbeat updates server liveness; sox/presence channel reflects agent as active.
Without heartbeat for the configured window, presence transitions to offline; recorded on sox/presence.
replay with since_seq=N returns only messages with seq>=N in monotone order.
replay with since_seq beyond last seq returns empty; no error.
Channel created under namespace A is not visible to list_channels under namespace B.
list_channels response includes _sox_protocol block with protocol_version matching spec/VERSION.
[pending] channels_collect returns when N replies arrive on the broadcast thread; SSE progress events emitted en route. Marked pending: skipped under --strict.

public_api: run(target: str, fixtures: list[Path], strict: bool) -> RunResult
class StdioTarget — speaks MCP framing to packages/python via subprocess
class HttpTarget — POSTs to /v1/ops/<op>; consumes /v1/stream SSE for wait_for_stream assertions
harness.live_recv_strategy: For HttpTarget: open a single SSE connection to GET /v1/stream per agent at fixture start (matches http-transport plan wire_format.live_recv=SSE). Each event is a JSON envelope; runner indexes by channel+seq for wait_for_stream assertions with bounded timeout. For StdioTarget: poll recv on a 50ms interval up to wait_for_stream.timeout_s.

files.purpose: Harness implementing load_fixtures, run, StdioTarget, HttpTarget, CLI.
Fake target fixtures, ephemeral http server fixture using the real adapter.
YAML loading, schema validation, pending flag handling.
Subprocess lifecycle, MCP framing, recv polling.
POST request shape, SSE consumption, wait_for_stream assertion semantics.
Pending fixtures skipped under --strict; counted under non-strict.
Per-fixture pass/fail diff formatting; exit code derivation.
Documents fixture format, how to add fixtures, how third-party impls register a target, --strict semantics.
PR workflow: matrix over [stdio, http]; spins up the http server for the http leg; runs conformance_runner --strict; uploads result artifact.

test_plan: Unit: load_fixtures parses every fixture in spec/conformance/ without error.
Unit: schema validation rejects malformed fixtures (missing sequence, unknown operation).
Unit: StdioTarget mocks subprocess and asserts MCP framing.
Unit: HttpTarget uses ASGITransport against the real http adapter; asserts SSE wait_for_stream resolves on matching seq.
Unit: --strict skips fixtures with pending:true; non-strict runs them and surfaces results separately.
Unit: RunResult diff formatter on subset-mismatch.
Integration: tools/conformance_runner.py --target http://localhost:<port> --strict exits 0 once the http transport is up.
risks: SSE consumption in tests can hang if the harness does not impose a wait_for_stream timeout; mitigated by mandatory timeout_s field with sane default.

Existing JSON scenarios under spec/conformance/scenarios/ overlap with new YAML fixtures; resolution: delete the JSON scenarios in this engagement and reference the YAML equivalents in PR description (no duplication).
channels_collect is x-status: planned; including it as a pending fixture keeps the surface visible without failing CI.
Cross-target parity: a fixture passing on stdio but failing on http indicates a transport bug, not a fixture bug; the runner reports per-target results to make this distinction visible.
build_order: category: ack-nack (validates the channels_ack-as-tool semantics most aggressively)
remaining categories: subscription-patterns, threading, groups, dms, identity-verification, sequence-monotonicity, presence, replay, namespace-isolation
exit_signals: Python reference impl passes 100% of fixtures via stdio
Python reference impl passes 100% of fixtures via HTTP
